meta.description: Helios Design System → Carbon Web Components migration mapping table. Each entry defines how a Helios component maps to its CWC equivalent, including attribute renames, slot transforms, event rewiring, confidence scores, and risk flags.

uiShell.description: UI Shell components are cds-header and cds-side-nav. These use position:fixed and must be rendered in their own document context (an iframe) to work correctly — they cannot be rendered inline inside an Ember component template.
uiShell.outputRule: If the migrated output contains cds-header or cds-side-nav, write the CWC output to showcase/public/sandbox-standalone.html only. The component-sandbox.gts file permanently renders a ShwFrame iframe pointing at /sandbox-standalone.html and must not be modified with inline CWC. If no UI Shell components are present, write CWC directly into component-sandbox.gts inline.

confidenceLevels.high: ≥ 0.90 — auto-apply in safe-only and full mode. RULE: manual-migration-required must NOT appear in riskFlags at this level — move any manual-case notes into the notes field instead.
confidenceLevels.medium: 0.60–0.89 — requires explicit user approval in full mode before applying

meta.noEquivalent: Some Helios components have no CWC custom element (cwcComponent: null). These migrate to native HTML elements styled with Carbon design token classes (e.g. cds--body-01, cds--heading-03) loaded via themes.css CDN.

Hds::Dropdown.description: Dropdown MENU component — a toggle-triggered popover containing action items. This is NOT a select/combobox. Prefer Carbon menu/menu-button primitives over overflow menu for this migration because overflow menu is a narrower pattern.

@isOpen.notes: @isOpen={{true}} maps to the open boolean attribute on cds-menu-button.

@isInline.notes: @isInline renders the trigger inline (block layout otherwise). cds-menu-button already behaves like an inline trigger control — remove.

@listPosition.notes: HDS @listPosition has no confirmed 1:1 cds-menu-button attribute mapping documented here. Treat positioning as a manual follow-up and preserve intent with the closest supported menu placement configuration in Carbon.

@width.notes: @width sets a CSS width on the menu surface. Apply via CSS on the migrated menu container.

@height.notes: @height sets a CSS max-height on the menu surface. Apply via CSS on the migrated menu container.

@enableCollisionDetection.notes: @enableCollisionDetection has no confirmed direct cds-menu-button attribute mapping documented here. Treat as a manual positioning/alignment follow-up.

@preserveContentInDom.notes: @preserveContentInDom keeps the dropdown content in the DOM when closed. CWC manages its own DOM lifecycle — remove.

@matchToggleWidth.notes: @matchToggleWidth makes the list as wide as the trigger. No CWC equivalent — remove and control width via CSS.

@onClose.notes: @onClose requires manual event wiring against the chosen Carbon menu implementation. Do not assume a direct close event parity without verifying the specific CWC event API in use.

@onFocusOut.notes: @onFocusOut maps to the native focusout event on the migrated menu trigger/container.

@boundary.notes: @boundary sets the scrolling container for collision detection. No CWC equivalent — remove.

click.notes: Menu item activation is handled through the click event on the migrated Carbon menu item/button element.

focusout.notes: Native focusout event on the migrated menu trigger/container. Replaces @onFocusOut.

ToggleButton.notes: D.ToggleButton becomes the visible cds-menu-button trigger. @text becomes the trigger label. Optional @icon requires a manual Carbon SVG substitution in the trigger.

ToggleIcon.notes: D.ToggleIcon (icon-only toggle, @text is the accessible label, @icon is the icon name, @hasChevron) is best represented by a Carbon icon-button style trigger paired with the menu. Use the tooltip/label content for accessibility and substitute the icon manually.

Interactive.notes: D.Interactive becomes <cds-menu-item> inside the migrated Carbon menu. @text → default slot content. @href → href when supported by the chosen item primitive, otherwise wrap with anchor behavior manually. @color='critical' requires a manual danger/destructive treatment decision. @isLoading → disabled (approximate). @icon/@trailingIcon require manual Carbon SVG substitution. @route/routing args → resolve to href.

Separator.notes: D.Separator becomes a standalone <cds-menu-item-divider> between adjacent menu items.

Checkbox.notes: D.Checkbox (checkbox list item with @id, @value, @icon, @count) requires manual restructuring with Carbon menu primitives or a more appropriate selection component.

Checkmark.notes: D.Checkmark should migrate to cds-menu-item with selected state and an explicit checkmark icon where appropriate. Preserve @selected manually and substitute any HDS icon/count behavior as needed.

Radio.notes: D.Radio (@id, @value, @icon, @count) requires manual restructuring with Carbon menu primitives or a radio-group pattern depending on behavior.

CopyItem.notes: D.CopyItem (@text required, @copyItemTitle, @isTruncated) copies text to clipboard. No CWC overflow-menu-item equivalent — implement as a cds-overflow-menu-item with a custom click handler that calls navigator.clipboard.writeText().

Title.notes: D.Title (@text required) renders a section heading. No CWC equivalent — omit or use a disabled cds-overflow-menu-item for a plain-text label.

Description.notes: D.Description (@text required) renders descriptive text. No CWC equivalent — omit or use a disabled cds-overflow-menu-item.

Header.notes: D.Header (arbitrary yielded content, optional @hasDivider) has no CWC equivalent — omit or restructure content outside the menu.

Footer.notes: D.Footer (arbitrary yielded content, optional @hasDivider) has no CWC equivalent — omit or restructure content outside the menu.

Generic.notes: D.Generic (arbitrary yielded content with consumer-owned layout/a11y) has no CWC equivalent — place custom content directly in a cds-overflow-menu-item or restructure outside the menu.

Hds::Dropdown.notes: LOW CONFIDENCE. Per review feedback, prefer Carbon menu/menu-button primitives over cds-overflow-menu for Hds::Dropdown because overflow menu is a narrower pattern. Treat this migration as manual-first. Recommended direction: cds-menu-button as the trigger, cds-menu-item for actionable entries, cds-menu-item-divider for separators, and selected-state handling on cds-menu-item for checkmark cases. D.CopyItem, D.Generic, D.Title, D.Description, D.Header, D.Footer, D.Checkbox, and D.Radio still require manual restructuring and should not be auto-applied.

Hds::AppFrame.description: Application layout wrapper providing Header, Sidebar, Main, Footer, and Modals named slots. No CWC equivalent — layout is handled by placing CWC UI Shell elements as siblings with CSS positioning.

@hasHeader.notes: @hasHeader (default true) controls rendering of the <header> container. No CWC equivalent — remove. If explicitly set to false, omit cds-header from the migrated template.

@hasSidebar.notes: @hasSidebar (default true) controls rendering of the <aside> container. No CWC equivalent — remove. If explicitly false, omit cds-side-nav from the migrated template.

@hasFooter.notes: @hasFooter (default true) controls rendering of the <footer> container. No CWC equivalent — remove. If explicitly false, omit the <footer> from the migrated template.

@hasModals.notes: @hasModals (default true) controls rendering of the modals <div> container. No CWC equivalent — remove. cds-modal elements do not need a dedicated mount point.

@hasMain.notes: @hasMain (default true) controls rendering of the <main> container. No CWC equivalent — remove. The main content area is always rendered; use a plain <main class='cds--content'> element directly.

Header.notes: AF.Header yields into a <header> HTML element. Its content (typically HdsAppHeader) becomes a standalone cds-header element. See Hds::AppHeader mapping.

Sidebar.notes: AF.Sidebar yields into an <aside> HTML element. Its content (typically HdsAppSideNav) becomes a standalone cds-side-nav element. See Hds::AppSideNav mapping.

Main.notes: AF.Main yields into a <main> element with default id='hds-main' (the skip link target for AppHeader's a11yRefocusSkipTo). Replace with <main class='cds--content' id='main-content'>. Update any cds-header skip-to link to point at the new id.

Footer.notes: AF.Footer yields into a <footer> element. Place footer content directly in a <footer> element. See Hds::AppFooter mapping for styling.

Modals.notes: AF.Modals yields into a <div> — a plain container for modal elements. cds-modal does not require a dedicated container; place cds-modal elements directly in the page template and remove the wrapper div entirely.

Hds::AppFrame.notes: No CWC equivalent. Remove HdsAppFrame entirely and restructure as sibling elements: cds-header + cds-side-nav + <main class='cds--content'> + <footer>. Key corrections: (1) @hasMain IS a real arg (default true) — if explicitly false, omit the <main> element from the migrated template; (2) AF.Sidebar yields into <aside>; (3) AF.Main has default id='hds-main' — preserve or update AppHeader skip link; (4) AF.Modals yields into a <div>, not a portal — cds-modal needs no mount point. CSS: cds-header ~ cds-side-nav { block-size: calc(100% - 3rem); margin-block-start: 3rem }.

Hds::PageHeader.description: Page-level header showing title, breadcrumb, icon, badges, subtitle, description, generic metadata, and actions. No CWC equivalent. Transforms entirely to native HTML with Carbon typography classes. HdsPageHeader has NO @args — only ...attributes and yielded contextual components.

PH.Title.notes:
PH.Title content is always rendered inside a hardcoded

in HDS — it is NOT configurable. Replace with

content

. Per HDS guidelines this must be the only

on the page. Do NOT downgrade to h2/h3 — the source rendered an h1 and the migration must preserve that semantic.

PH.Breadcrumb.notes: PH.Breadcrumb is a generic yield — conventionally used to place an HdsBreadcrumb inside. Replace the wrapper with a <nav aria-label='breadcrumb'> and migrate the inner HdsBreadcrumb separately. If a cds-breadcrumb CWC component is available in your version, use that instead.

PH.IconTile.notes: PH.IconTile yields an HdsIconTile with @size pre-bound to 'medium'. No CWC equivalent — replace with a custom <span> or <div> containing an appropriate Carbon SVG icon, or omit if purely decorative.

PH.Badges.notes: PH.Badges is a yield block intended for one or more HdsBadge components. Replace with a <div class='cds--page-header__badges'> containing cds-tag elements (see Hds::Badge mapping). Supports ...attributes.

PH.Subtitle.notes:
PH.Subtitle content becomes a

or depending on context. Content can be plain text or structured. The text style is inherited from the slot — apply Carbon typography class to the wrapper element.

PH.Description.notes:
PH.Description content becomes a

. Content can be plain text or structured (links, inline elements). Supports ...attributes.

PH.Generic.notes: PH.Generic is a yield block for arbitrary metadata content (key/value pairs, custom structured data). Renders after Subtitle and Description. No inherited text style — consumer controls layout. Replace with a <div> containing the custom content.

PH.Actions.notes: PH.Actions is a yield block for page-level buttons and dropdowns. Replace with a <div class='cds--page-header__actions'> containing the appropriate migrated Carbon button/menu primitives. Supports ...attributes.

Hds::PageHeader.notes: Manual migration only. HdsPageHeader has no CWC equivalent and should not be automatically swapped. Key corrections: (1) HdsPageHeader has NO @args — remove the 'as |PH|' entry that was previously listed as an attribute to remove (it doesn't exist); (2) PH.Title always renders as <h1> — do NOT change the heading level; (3) all 8 contextual components are yield blocks requiring hand-authored replacement structure. Replace the entire HdsPageHeader block manually with native HTML and Carbon typography/layout classes after reviewing the specific page composition.

Hds::AppSideNav::List.description: A grouped list of navigation links inside the side nav. Wrapped in a <nav> element. Yields ExtraBefore, Item, BackLink, Title, Link, ExtraAfter contextual components. In practice used inside AppSideNav::Portal.

Title.notes: L.Title yields inner content (not a @text arg) as a visible section label. cds-side-nav-items has no title sub-component — use a cds-side-nav-menu as the nearest equivalent for grouped sections (it acts as a collapsible group header), or omit entirely.

Link.notes: L.Link becomes a cds-side-nav-link. Args: @text → default slot content; @href → href attribute (direct); @icon (HDS icon name) → Carbon SVG in slot='title-icon'; @isActive → active boolean attribute; @isHrefExternal={{true}} → adds target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer' AND renders a trailing external-link icon in HDS (no CWC equivalent for the icon — drop it); @badge (string) → no CWC equivalent, drop; @count (string) → no CWC equivalent, drop; @hasSubItems → use cds-side-nav-menu instead. L.Link also yields content after the leading block — no CWC equivalent for this slot. Routing args (@route etc.) → resolve to plain href.

BackLink.notes: L.BackLink (@text, @href, @isHrefExternal, routing args) is a back-navigation link. Replace with a cds-side-nav-link containing a back-arrow Carbon SVG in slot='title-icon'. @text → default slot content. @href/@route → resolve to href.

Item.notes: L.Item yields into an <li> element — generic non-link content. Place content directly inside cds-side-nav-items as a child element.

ExtraBefore.notes: L.ExtraBefore injects arbitrary content before the <ul> list but inside the <nav> wrapper. Place directly before the cds-side-nav-link elements inside cds-side-nav-items.

ExtraAfter.notes: L.ExtraAfter injects arbitrary content after the <ul> list but inside the <nav> wrapper. Place directly after the cds-side-nav-link elements inside cds-side-nav-items.

Hds::AppSideNav::List.notes: Low-medium confidence. L.Title yields content (not a @text arg). L.Link maps to cds-side-nav-link but @icon requires a Carbon SVG in slot='title-icon', @badge/@count are dropped, @hasSubItems means use cds-side-nav-menu. L.BackLink → cds-side-nav-link with back-arrow icon. L.Item yields into <li>. @isHrefExternal trailing icon has no CWC equivalent. HdsAppSideNavList itself has no args — all args are on its contextual sub-components.

Hds::Form.description: Form container component. Maps to cds-form. NOTE: HdsForm is a complex contextual component with many sub-components (Section, SectionHeader, Footer, Separator, etc.) — most have no direct CWC equivalent.

@tag.notes: @tag accepts 'form' (default) or 'div', controlling the rendered HTML element. cds-form always renders as a <form>. If @tag='div' is used, replace with a plain <div> instead of cds-form.

@sectionMaxWidth.notes: @sectionMaxWidth sets a CSS max-width on the form sections. No CWC equivalent — apply via a CSS custom property or inline style on the cds-form element.

as |F|.notes: Block param syntax (as |F|) is Glimmer-specific. Remove entirely — cds-form has no contextual components.

F.Header.notes: F.Header (with sub-components F.HeaderTitle, F.HeaderDescription) has no CWC equivalent. Replace with a plain <div> or <header> containing heading and paragraph elements with Carbon typography classes.

F.Section.notes: F.Section (with sub-components F.SectionHeader, F.SectionHeaderTitle, F.SectionHeaderDescription, F.SectionMultiFieldGroup, F.SectionMultiFieldGroupItem) becomes a plain <div class="cds--form-item"> or <fieldset> as a direct child of cds-form. None of the Section sub-components have CWC equivalents.

F.Separator.notes: F.Separator (a visual divider between sections) has no CWC equivalent. Replace with an <hr> element or a CSS border.

F.Footer.notes: F.Footer (with sub-component FF.ButtonSet) becomes a plain <div class="cds--form-actions"> or similar wrapper. FF.ButtonSet → cds-button-set.

Hds::Form.notes: Confidence downgraded to 0.55 (low-medium). The outer cds-form tag swap is simple, but HdsForm has a large contextual component API (Header, HeaderTitle, HeaderDescription, Section, SectionHeader, SectionHeaderTitle, SectionHeaderDescription, SectionMultiFieldGroup, SectionMultiFieldGroupItem, Separator, Footer) — none of these have CWC equivalents. Each must be replaced with plain HTML + Carbon typography/layout classes. @tag='div' means skip cds-form entirely. @sectionMaxWidth requires CSS. Do not treat this as a simple tag swap.

Hds::AppFooter.description: Global page footer. No CWC equivalent in @carbon/web-components — transforms to a native HTML <footer> element styled with Carbon design tokens.

@ariaLabel.notes: @ariaLabel (default 'Footer items') is applied to the <ul> list of footer links, NOT to the <footer> element itself. On the replacement: pass as aria-label on the <ul> element wrapping the footer links.

@copyrightYear.notes: @copyrightYear overrides the auto-generated current year in the copyright notice. Only needs migration if a custom year was explicitly passed — otherwise the auto-year logic must be replicated (e.g. new Date().getFullYear()) in the replacement template.

@theme.notes: @theme accepts 'light' (default) or 'dark'. Apply the corresponding Carbon theme data attribute to the <footer> element: 'light' → no attribute needed (Carbon default); 'dark' → data-carbon-theme='g100' (or g90 depending on the dark theme variant).

AF.ExtraBefore.notes: AF.ExtraBefore yields arbitrary content injected before the <ul> list of footer links. Place as a direct sibling before the <ul> inside the <footer>.

AF.StatusLink.notes:
AF.StatusLink is a link with a status indicator. Args: @status enum ('operational'|'degraded'|'maintenance'|'outage') auto-sets text/icon/color; @statusIcon overrides the icon name; @statusIconColor overrides the icon color (any CSS color); @text overrides the label text; @href/@isHrefExternal for the link URL; routing args (@route etc.) for Ember links. Replace with an
  • All systems operational
    • . Color map: operational → var(--cds-support-success), degraded → var(--cds-support-warning), maintenance → var(--cds-support-info), outage → var(--cds-support-error).

AF.LegalLinks.notes:
AF.LegalLinks renders a pre-built set of legal links (Support, Terms of Service, Privacy, Security, Accessibility) with overridable hrefs. Args: @hrefForSupport (default 'https://www.hashicorp.com/support'), @hrefForTerms (default hashicorp ToS — MUST be overridden per product), @hrefForPrivacy, @hrefForSecurity, @hrefForCookies. Also has @ariaLabel (default 'Legal links'). Replace with
  • Support
  • Terms
    • ...
.

AF.Link.notes:
AF.Link yields into an element. Args: @href/@isHrefExternal for external links (adds target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer'); routing args (@route etc.) for internal Ember links; @icon (any icon name) and @iconPosition ('leading'|'trailing', default trailing). Replace with
  • content
    • . @icon has no CWC link equivalent — drop icon or render a Carbon SVG inline adjacent to the link text.

AF.Item.notes: AF.Item yields into an <li> element — used for custom non-link content. Replace with a plain <li> containing the custom content. Supports ...attributes.

AF.ExtraAfter.notes: AF.ExtraAfter yields arbitrary content injected after the <ul> list of footer links. Place as a direct sibling after the <ul> inside the <footer>.

Hds::AppFooter.notes: No CWC custom element. Replace <HdsAppFooter> with a plain <footer>. Key corrections: (1) @ariaLabel applies to the <ul> list, not the <footer> element; (2) AF.LegalLinks has pre-built links with overridable hrefs — document which URLs are being used, especially @hrefForTerms which MUST be product-specific; (3) AF.StatusLink has a @status enum with 4 values that auto-set icon/color/text — map to Carbon support tokens; (4) AF.Link yields into an <a> directly, @icon is dropped; (5) AF.Item yields into an <li>; (6) @copyrightYear only needs migration if a custom year was passed — otherwise replicate with JS date.

Hds::Badge.description: Badge/tag component for static labels and status indicators. HdsBadge is non-interactive only. Note: HDS has a separate Hds::Tag component for dismissible/interactive use cases. CWC tag variants: cds-tag (read-only, default open=true), cds-dismissible-tag (user-dismissible), cds-selectable-tag (toggle, no color), cds-operational-tag (toggle with type/color).

@text.notes: @text (required, string or number) must be placed as default slot content on cds-tag — cds-tag has NO text attribute or property. Example: <cds-tag>{{@text}}</cds-tag>. Note: cds-dismissible-tag, cds-selectable-tag, and cds-operational-tag DO have a text attribute — this correction applies to cds-tag only.

@type.notes: HDS @type ('filled' default, 'inverted', 'outlined') is a fill style. IMPORTANT: CWC cds-tag's type attribute is a COLOR NAME (gray, red, green…) — not a fill style. There is no CWC equivalent for fill style. 'filled' → use cds-tag as-is (default). 'inverted' → no equivalent; approximate with CSS or a dark Carbon theme context. 'outlined' → no equivalent; cds-tag is always filled. This is a lossy migration — @type information is dropped.

@color.notes: HDS @color (semantic) maps to CWC type (palette color name). Confirmed CWC TAG_TYPE values include: gray, red, magenta, purple, blue, cyan, teal, green, cool-gray, warm-gray. Mapping: 'neutral' → 'gray', 'neutral-dark-mode' → 'cool-gray' (approximate), 'highlight' → 'purple', 'success' → 'green', 'warning' → 'warm-gray' (Carbon has no yellow — warm-gray is closest, verify visually), 'critical' → 'red'. Default on both sides is neutral/gray.

@size.notes: HDS @size: 'small' | 'medium' (default) | 'large'. CWC TAG_SIZE: 'sm' | 'md' (default) | 'lg'. All three map directly and losslessly: small → sm, medium → md, large → lg.

@isInteractive.notes: HdsBadge @isInteractive is not a real arg — HdsBadge is always non-interactive. For interactive badge-like elements HDS uses Hds::Tag instead. If source has a badge that needs toggle behaviour, use cds-selectable-tag (no color support) or cds-operational-tag (has type/color, fires cds-operational-tag-selected). cds-interactive-tag does NOT exist in CWC v2.

@icon.notes: @icon accepts an HDS icon name string — icons always display in the leading position. cds-tag has no icon name attribute. Set has-custom-icon boolean on cds-tag and place a Carbon SVG as a child element (it will render in the leading position). No automatic HDS icon name → Carbon SVG mapping exists — manual SVG substitution required.

@isIconOnly.notes: @isIconOnly=true shows only the icon; @text is still required for screen readers (rendered as aria-label in HDS). On cds-tag: set has-custom-icon, place the Carbon SVG as a child, omit text from the default slot, and add aria-label matching @text on the cds-tag element for accessibility.

default.notes: Text content passes through as default slot children of cds-tag. This is the only supported mechanism for text on cds-tag — there is no text attribute on cds-tag itself.

Hds::Badge.notes: Confidence raised to 0.65. @text must go in the default slot — cds-tag has no text attribute (unlike cds-dismissible-tag, cds-selectable-tag, cds-operational-tag which do). @size maps cleanly: small → sm, medium → md, large → lg (all three exist in TAG_SIZE). Core @color → type mapping is correct but approximate — CWC types are palette colors, HDS colors are semantic. The @type fill-style axis (filled/inverted/outlined) is entirely lost — cds-tag has no fill style concept. @icon requires manual SVG substitution + has-custom-icon attribute. cds-tag-beingclosed/cds-tag-closed events only fire when filter=true on cds-tag, which is not relevant for HdsBadge (non-interactive). If @isInteractive is needed, use cds-selectable-tag or cds-operational-tag.

Hds::Alert.description: Alert/notification component for user feedback. The correct CWC target component depends on the HDS @type value — see @type notes below.

@type.notes: @type is the Helios display VARIANT — accepted values are 'page', 'inline', 'compact'. Choose the CWC tag based on this value: 'inline' → cds-inline-notification, 'compact' → cds-inline-notification with low-contrast boolean attribute, 'page' → cds-actionable-notification. Do NOT map @type to kind.

@color.notes: @color maps to kind on the CWC notification. CWC kind accepts: error | info | success | warning. 'neutral' and 'highlight' both map to 'info'. 'critical' → 'error'. Note: CWC kind defaults to 'success' — always set kind explicitly.

@icon.notes: @icon accepts an HDS icon name string to override the default severity icon, or false to hide it. CWC notifications always show a fixed status icon matching the kind — there is no icon override attribute. If @icon={{false}}, add hide-close-button to suppress the close button but the status icon cannot be hidden.

@onDismiss.notes: HDS @onDismiss fires when the user clicks the dismiss button. CWC fires two events: cds-notification-beingclosed (cancellable, fires BEFORE close) and cds-notification-closed (fires AFTER close). Wire @onDismiss to cds-notification-beingclosed: {{on 'cds-notification-beingclosed' this.onDismiss}}. To suppress the dismiss button entirely, add the hide-close-button boolean attribute. To programmatically dismiss, set open=false on the element.

cds-notification-beingclosed.notes: Fires before the notification is closed by user gesture. Cancellable — call event.preventDefault() to block the close. This is the correct event to wire to @onDismiss.

cds-notification-closed.notes: Fires after the notification has been closed by user gesture. Use this for post-dismiss side effects (e.g. clearing state), not for blocking the close.

Title.notes:
A.Title content becomes a child element in slot='title' on the CWC notification. A.Title accepts a @tag arg ('div' default, or 'h1'–'h6') — use the same tag for the slot wrapper (e.g.

text

). Both cds-inline-notification and cds-actionable-notification have a title named slot.

Description.notes: A.Description content becomes a child element in slot='subtitle'. A.Description accepts complex content (HTML, conditionals) — preserve rich children inside the slot wrapper. Both CWC notification types have a subtitle named slot.

Button.notes: A.Button (HdsButton with size='small', color limited to 'secondary'/'tertiary') has no equivalent on cds-inline-notification. Switch to cds-actionable-notification and set action-button-label to the button text. For richer action buttons, use cds-callout-notification which has a dedicated action slot.

LinkStandalone.notes: A.LinkStandalone (HdsLinkStandalone with size='small') has no CWC notification equivalent. Switch to cds-actionable-notification or place the link outside the notification.

GenericContent.notes: A.GenericContent yields arbitrary unstyled content below Title/Description and above actions. cds-inline-notification and cds-actionable-notification only support title/subtitle slots — use cds-callout-notification (which has an action slot for richer content) or restructure content outside the notification.

GenericFooter.notes: A.GenericFooter yields arbitrary unstyled content at the bottom. No CWC notification equivalent — use cds-callout-notification's action slot or place content below the notification.

Hds::Alert.notes: Medium confidence. The CWC tag depends on HDS @type: 'inline' → cds-inline-notification, 'compact' → cds-inline-notification + low-contrast, 'page' → cds-actionable-notification. For action buttons use cds-actionable-notification (action-button-label attr) or cds-callout-notification (action slot). @color → kind maps cleanly (error|info|success|warning). Dismissal: wire @onDismiss to cds-notification-beingclosed (cancellable) not cds-notification-closed (post-close). hide-close-button suppresses the dismiss button. open=false programmatically closes. A.Title/@tag, A.Button/A.LinkStandalone/A.GenericContent/A.GenericFooter all require manual restructuring.

Hds::AppSideNav.description: Application side navigation panel, optionally collapsible and responsive. Content is injected via AppSideNav::Portal (ember-stargate) into AppSideNav::PortalTarget — not via direct slot children.

@isResponsive.notes: @isResponsive (default true) maps to collapse-mode on cds-side-nav. true → collapse-mode='responsive', false → collapse-mode='fixed'.

@isCollapsible.notes: @isCollapsible (default false) enables the hamburger toggle on large viewports. Only has effect when @isResponsive is also true. In CWC, add a cds-header-menu-button inside cds-header — the toggle wiring to cds-side-nav is automatic when they are siblings.

@isMinimized.notes: @isMinimized (default false) — when true maps to collapsed state on cds-side-nav (absence of expanded attribute). @isMinimized={{false}} → add expanded attribute. Note: per HDS docs, after initial render this arg tracks internal state and should not be used to control state from outside.

@breakpoint.notes: @breakpoint (default '1088px') sets the viewport width for mobile/desktop transition. cds-side-nav uses Carbon's internal breakpoint — remove.

@onToggleMinimizedStatus.notes: @onToggleMinimizedStatus (isMinimized: boolean) fires on collapse/expand. In CWC listen to cds-header-menu-button-toggled on cds-header-menu-button — the event fires from the button, not from cds-side-nav.

@onDesktopViewportChange.notes: @onDesktopViewportChange (isDesktop: boolean) fires when viewport crosses the breakpoint. No CWC equivalent — implement via ResizeObserver or a CSS media query listener.

cds-header-menu-button-toggled.notes: Fires from cds-header-menu-button (not cds-side-nav) when the hamburger is toggled. Replaces @onToggleMinimizedStatus.

default.notes: HdsAppSideNav yields into a <div>. In practice, nav content is NOT placed directly here — it is injected via AppSideNav::Portal (ember-stargate) into AppSideNav::PortalTarget. On migration, replace the Portal/PortalTarget pattern with direct cds-side-nav-items children inside cds-side-nav.

Portal.notes: AppSideNav::Portal transports content (an AppSideNav::List) via ember-stargate into AppSideNav::PortalTarget. The Portal has @targetName (default 'hds-app-side-nav-portal-target') and @ariaLabel (applied to the <nav> in the List). On migration: remove the Portal/PortalTarget indirection entirely and place cds-side-nav-items directly inside cds-side-nav. Move the @ariaLabel to an aria-label attribute on cds-side-nav.

Hds::AppSideNav.notes: Confidence adjusted to 0.65. Key additions: (1) HdsAppSideNav yields into a <div>; (2) the Portal/PortalTarget pattern (ember-stargate) is the real content injection mechanism — consumers use AppSideNav::Portal not direct slot children; (3) on migration, remove the Portal/PortalTarget indirection and place cds-side-nav-items directly in cds-side-nav; (4) @ariaLabel from AppSideNav::Portal moves to aria-label on cds-side-nav; (5) @isCollapsible only has effect when @isResponsive is also true; (6) the hamburger toggle is a cds-header-menu-button in cds-header, not on cds-side-nav.

@size.notes: HDS @size ('small' | 'medium' | 'large') maps to MODAL_SIZE on cds-modal ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg'). CWC default is 'md', matching HDS default of 'medium'.

@color.notes: HDS @color accepts 'neutral' (default), 'warning', OR 'critical' — all three are real values. cds-modal has no color attribute for neutral/warning — remove those. For @color='critical', add the alert boolean attribute to cds-modal: <cds-modal alert>. This triggers Carbon's danger/alert modal styling. 'warning' has no CWC equivalent — remove and handle via content.

@isDismissDisabled.notes: @isDismissDisabled prevents ALL dismissal (Escape key, click outside, close button). On cds-modal you need TWO attributes to fully replicate this: (1) prevent-close-on-click-outside — blocks click-outside dismissal; (2) prevent-close — blocks the close button. Additionally listen to cds-modal-beingclosed and call event.preventDefault() to block Escape key dismissal. All three are needed together.

@onOpen.notes: No cds-modal-opened event exists on cds-modal. To detect when the modal opens, watch the open attribute with a Glimmer modifier or use a MutationObserver on the element.

@onClose.notes: HDS @onClose receives the close Event as argument. Replace with {{on 'cds-modal-closed' this.closeModal}} on the cds-modal element. cds-modal-closed fires after the modal has fully closed. If you need to react before close (e.g. to block it), use cds-modal-beingclosed instead.

@returnFocusTo.notes: @returnFocusTo accepts an element ID string to restore focus to on close. cds-modal manages focus return automatically. Remove this arg — if a non-default element needs focus after close, call element.focus() manually inside the cds-modal-closed event handler.

cds-modal-beingclosed.notes: Fires before the modal is closed by user gesture. Cancellable — call event.preventDefault() to block the close. Use this to implement @isDismissDisabled behaviour alongside prevent-close and prevent-close-on-click-outside.

cds-modal-closed.notes: Fires after the modal has been closed by user gesture. Replaces @onClose. Wire via {{on 'cds-modal-closed' this.handler}}.

Header.notes: M.Header (backed by HdsDialogPrimitiveHeader, yields @onDismiss) becomes <cds-modal-header><cds-modal-heading>title text</cds-modal-heading></cds-modal-header>. The close button is built into cds-modal-header automatically — no need to wire @onDismiss manually.

Body.notes: M.Body (backed by HdsDialogPrimitiveBody) becomes <cds-modal-body><cds-modal-body-content>...</cds-modal-body-content></cds-modal-body>. If body content scrolls, add has-scrolling-content to cds-modal.

Footer.notes: M.Footer (backed by HdsDialogPrimitiveFooter, yields MF.close) becomes <cds-modal-footer>. Place cds-modal-footer-button elements inside (same API as cds-button). To wire a close/cancel button: listen to cds-modal-beingclosed on cds-modal OR set open=false on the element directly — there is NO data-modal-close attribute on cds-modal-footer-button.

openPattern.notes: Remove the {{#if}} block — use the open attribute (default false) directly on cds-modal instead. Set open=true to show, open=false to hide.

Hds::Modal.notes: Medium confidence. @size maps directly (sm/md/lg). @color: 'neutral'/'warning' are removed (no CWC equivalent); 'critical' → alert boolean attribute on cds-modal. @isDismissDisabled requires THREE CWC mechanisms: prevent-close + prevent-close-on-click-outside attributes + cds-modal-beingclosed cancellation. @onClose → cds-modal-closed event. @onOpen has no CWC event. Contextual slots (M.Header/Body/Footer) become explicit child elements (cds-modal-header, cds-modal-body, cds-modal-footer). Footer buttons use cds-modal-footer-button (same API as cds-button). data-modal-close does NOT exist — close via open=false or event handling. v2.60.0 changes: prevent-close and prevent-close-on-click-outside moved to CDSModalBase (inherited by CDSModal) — they still work identically as HTML attributes; no migration change needed. New enable-dialog-element boolean attribute added to cds-modal — do NOT set this during migration (switches rendering to native <dialog> element, which is an opt-in behaviour change).

Hds::Accordion.description: Accordion component for collapsible content sections

@size.notes: HDS @size ('small' | 'medium' | 'large') maps to ACCORDION_SIZE on cds-accordion ('sm' | 'md' | 'lg'). CWC default is 'md', matching HDS default of 'medium'. Note: size is set on cds-accordion itself (not per-item).

@type.notes: HDS @type accepts 'card' (default) or 'flush' — NOT 'button'. 'flush' maps directly to the isFlush boolean attribute on cds-accordion. 'card' (default) → use cds-accordion without isFlush. Note: isFlush does not work when alignment='start' on cds-accordion.

@forceState.notes: HDS @forceState on the parent forces all items 'open' or 'close'. cds-accordion has no group-level force-state — set the open boolean attribute on each cds-accordion-item individually to replicate this.

@titleTag.notes: HDS @titleTag controls the heading element for the toggle ('div' default | 'h1'–'h6'). cds-accordion-item manages its own heading semantics internally — remove this arg.

cds-accordion-item-beingtoggled.notes: Fires before a cds-accordion-item is toggled by user gesture. Cancellable — call event.preventDefault() to block the toggle. Replaces A.Item @onClickToggle (partially — @onClickToggle cannot cancel; this event can).

cds-accordion-item-toggled.notes: Fires after a cds-accordion-item has been toggled. Use this for post-toggle side effects. Equivalent to A.Item @onClickToggle for non-cancelling use cases.

Item.notes: A.Item contextual component becomes <cds-accordion-item>. A.Item args: @isOpen → open boolean; @forceState='open'/'close' → open boolean (override after render); @disabled → disabled boolean; @ariaLabel (default 'Toggle display') → no direct CWC equivalent, remove; @isStatic → no CWC equivalent (disabled greys out the item but does not hide the chevron — see note); @containsInteractive → no CWC equivalent, remove.

toggle.notes: The <:toggle>content</:toggle> named block becomes the title string attribute on cds-accordion-item. LOSSY: cds-accordion-item title is a plain string only — rich content (HTML, components) in the toggle block cannot be preserved. Flatten to plain text. [C].close (a function to programmatically close the item) has no CWC equivalent — remove any usages.

content.notes: The <:content>...</:content> named block becomes direct children of cds-accordion-item.

Hds::Accordion.notes: Confidence adjusted to 0.72. Key corrections: (1) HDS @type is 'card' (default) | 'flush' — NOT 'button'/'card'. 'flush' maps to the isFlush boolean on cds-accordion. (2) cds-accordion has events: cds-accordion-item-beingtoggled (cancellable) and cds-accordion-item-toggled. (3) A.Item has several args with no CWC equivalent: @isStatic (static/non-interactive toggle), @containsInteractive, @ariaLabel — all must be dropped. (4) :toggle block content must be flattened to plain text for the title attribute — rich toggle content is not supported. (5) [C].close function has no CWC equivalent.

Hds::AppHeader.description: Top application header bar with logo, navigation, and utility action named blocks.

@hasA11yRefocus.notes: @hasA11yRefocus (default true) controls the ember-a11y-refocus skip link and navigator narrator. No CWC equivalent. IMPORTANT: if this was explicitly set to false in the source, that means the team knowingly disabled Bypass Blocks (WCAG 2.4.1) — flag this as an accessibility debt in the migration report rather than silently removing it.

@breakpoint.notes: @breakpoint (default '1088px') sets the viewport width where the header switches between mobile and desktop views. cds-header uses Carbon's internal breakpoint system — remove.

@a11yRefocusSkipTo.notes: @a11yRefocusSkipTo (default '#hds-main') is the element ID that the skip link focuses. This default matches AppFrame::Main's default id='hds-main'. No CWC equivalent. When removing, ensure there is still a visible skip link mechanism if needed for accessibility.

@a11yRefocusSkipText.notes: @a11yRefocusSkipText (default 'Skip to main content') is the skip link text. No CWC equivalent — remove. If a custom value was set, note it as a manual a11y follow-up.

@a11yRefocusNavigationText.notes: @a11yRefocusNavigationText is the screen reader message after navigation completes. No CWC equivalent — remove.

@a11yRefocusRouteChangeValidator.notes: @a11yRefocusRouteChangeValidator is a custom function controlling which route changes trigger refocus. No CWC equivalent — remove.

@a11yRefocusExcludeAllQueryParams.notes: @a11yRefocusExcludeAllQueryParams opts out of all query param transition focus management. No CWC equivalent — remove.

logo.notes: The :logo named block (yields { close }) contains HdsAppHeaderHomeLink. Replace with cds-header-name inside cds-header. See Hds::AppHeader::HomeLink mapping for the HomeLink → cds-header-name transform.

globalActions.notes: The :globalActions named block (yields { close }) for org/project switcher becomes a cds-header-global-action with a panel-id attribute wired to a cds-header-panel containing a cds-switcher. The yielded { close } callback has no CWC equivalent — remove usages.

utilityActions.notes: The :utilityActions named block (yields { close }) for help/user/search actions becomes one or more cds-header-global-action elements inside a div.cds--header__global wrapper inside cds-header. The yielded { close } callback has no CWC equivalent — remove usages.

Hds::AppHeader.notes: Medium confidence. Key corrections: (1) @hasA11yRefocus default is true — if explicitly false in source, flag as accessibility debt (Bypass Blocks WCAG 2.4.1); (2) @a11yRefocusSkipTo default '#hds-main' connects to AppFrame::Main's default id — removing it means the skip link mechanism is lost unless replicated separately; (3) all three named blocks yield { close } which has no CWC equivalent — remove close usages. The :logo block becomes cds-header-name. Utility actions become cds-header-global-action elements. Org switcher becomes a cds-header-global-action + cds-header-panel + cds-switcher.

Hds::Text::Body.description: Body text component. No CWC custom element — transforms to a native HTML element with a Carbon body type class. Note: there are three HDS Text variants (Display, Body, Code) — this mapping covers Body only.

@tag.notes: Use the @tag value as the rendered HTML element. HDS default is 'span' (not div or p). If no @tag was set in the source, the element rendered as a <span> — preserve that. Accepted values: any valid HTML tag name (span, p, div, h1–h6, pre, code, etc.).

@size.notes: HDS Body @size accepts '300', '200' (default), or '100'. Map to Carbon typography classes: '300' → cds--body-02 (16px), '200' → cds--body-01 (14px, default), '100' → cds--helper-text-01 (12px). If no @size was set, use cds--body-01.

@weight.notes: HDS Body @weight accepts 'regular' (default), 'medium', or 'semibold'. No direct Carbon class equivalent — apply via inline style (style='font-weight: 500' for medium, 600 for semibold) or a CSS utility class. If no @weight was set, the element inherits weight from context (no inline style needed).

@align.notes: HDS @align accepts 'left', 'center', or 'right'. No Carbon class equivalent — apply via inline style (style='text-align: center') or a utility class. If no @align was set, alignment is inherited from context.

@color.notes: HDS @color accepts predefined semantic token names (primary, strong, faint, disabled, high-contrast, action, action-hover, action-active, highlight, success, warning, critical, and -on-surface/-high-contrast variants) OR any valid CSS color string (hex, rgb, var(--token-...) etc.). If a token name: map to the nearest Carbon text token via CSS custom property (e.g. 'primary' → var(--cds-text-primary), 'strong' → var(--cds-text-primary), 'faint' → var(--cds-text-helper), 'disabled' → var(--cds-text-disabled), 'action' → var(--cds-link-primary)). If a raw CSS string: pass through as inline style. If no @color was set, color is inherited from context.

default.notes: Inner content (plain text, HTML elements, or other components) passes through unchanged as children of the replacement element.

Hds::Text::Body.notes:
No CWC custom element. Replace text with

text

. Size class mapping: '200' (default) → cds--body-01, '300' → cds--body-02, '100' → cds--helper-text-01. IMPORTANT: default @tag is 'span' — if no @tag was set, render as . @weight/@align/@color have no Carbon class equivalents — use inline styles or omit if inherited from context. @color accepts both token names and raw CSS strings — token names map to Carbon CSS custom properties.

Hds::AppHeader::HomeLink.description: Home/logo link inside the app header. Typically placed in the :logo named block of HdsAppHeader.

@icon.notes: @icon is required and accepts an HDS icon name string (e.g. @icon='hashicorp'). cds-header-name has no icon slot — place a Carbon SVG or as a child element. The SVG/image should come before the text content.

@text.notes: @text is required. When @isIconOnly is true (the default), @text becomes the aria-label on the <a> tag — NOT visible text. When @isIconOnly={{false}}, @text is rendered visibly adjacent to the icon. On cds-header-name, text is always the default slot content — use hide-label or CSS to suppress visibility if icon-only display is needed.

@isIconOnly.notes: @isIconOnly defaults to TRUE in HDS — most usages render icon-only with @text as accessible aria-label only. cds-header-name always renders text visibly. Migration options: (1) if @isIconOnly=true (default), pass @text as aria-label on a wrapping <a> and place the SVG logo inside cds-header-name without visible text; (2) if @isIconOnly={{false}}, text was intentionally visible — place it as the default slot content of cds-header-name.

@color.notes: @color accepts any valid CSS color for the icon/text. cds-header-name styling is controlled by Carbon's theme — remove. If a custom color is essential, apply via CSS on the cds-header-name element.

@route.notes: @route (and related routing args: @models, @model, @query, @current-when, @replace, @isRouteExternal) are Ember LinkTo args. Replace with a plain href attribute on cds-header-name.

Hds::AppHeader::HomeLink.notes: Medium-high confidence. IMPORTANT: @isIconOnly defaults to true in HDS — the typical usage is icon-only with @text as accessible label only. cds-header-name always shows text; handle this via aria-label on the link or CSS text hiding. @href maps directly. @icon (required) needs a Carbon SVG child element. @color → CSS only. Routing args → plain href.

Hds::Form::TextInput::Field.description: Text input field with label, helper text, and error message

@type.notes: HDS accepts: text, email, password, url, search, date, time, datetime-local, month, week, tel. All map directly to INPUT_TYPE on cds-text-input. Note: @isLoading only applies to @type='search' in HDS.

@id.notes: @id sets an explicit id on the input control. Passes through directly to cds-text-input. If omitted, HDS auto-generates an id — cds-text-input does not, so downstream label associations may break if id is absent.

@isOptional.notes: @isOptional appends an '(Optional)' indicator next to the label. cds-text-input has no equivalent — remove and add the word 'Optional' directly into the label text if needed.

@isInvalid.notes: HDS @isInvalid is a boolean. CWC cds-text-input DOES have a matching invalid boolean attribute (property({ type: Boolean, reflect: true })). Direct rename: @isInvalid={{true}} → invalid on cds-text-input. Note: in HDS, invalid styling is separate from the error message (Field.Error block). In CWC, the invalid boolean attribute controls styling independently of the validity-message slot — both can coexist. If a Field.Error block is present, also populate the validity-message slot with the error text.

@isLoading.notes: @isLoading shows a loading spinner only when @type='search'. cds-text-input has no loading state — remove and handle loading at the form level if needed.

@hasVisibilityToggle.notes: HDS @hasVisibilityToggle defaults to TRUE for password fields. CWC show-password-visibility-toggle defaults to FALSE. Migration direction: for password inputs, explicitly add show-password-visibility-toggle to cds-text-input. If @hasVisibilityToggle={{false}} was set to suppress it, simply omit show-password-visibility-toggle on CWC (it is off by default).

@visibilityToggleAriaLabel.notes: HDS @visibilityToggleAriaLabel is a single label for the toggle button. CWC has two separate JS properties: showPasswordLabel (when password is hidden, default 'Show password') and hidePasswordLabel (when password is visible, default 'Hide password'). IMPORTANT: these are bare property() decorators with no explicit attribute — they are JS-property-only and cannot be set via HTML attributes in a template. They must be set programmatically: element.showPasswordLabel = 'Show'; element.hidePasswordLabel = 'Hide'. Map the HDS value to showPasswordLabel; set hidePasswordLabel separately if needed.

@visibilityToggleAriaMessageText.notes: @visibilityToggleAriaMessageText sets an aria-live message when the toggle is pressed (default 'Input content is hidden'). cds-text-input has no equivalent aria-live message for the visibility toggle — remove.

@width.notes: @width sets a fixed CSS width on the input. cds-text-input has no width attribute — by default it fills its container (isFluid behavior). Apply a fixed width via CSS on the cds-text-input element directly.

@extraAriaDescribedBy.notes: Extra aria-describedby IDs to append. Map directly to aria-describedby on cds-text-input. Note: HDS auto-generates aria-describedby from helper text and error IDs — on CWC this wiring is also automatic for the helper-text and validity-message slots, so only pass truly extra IDs here.

invalid.notes: CWC cds-text-input fires a native invalid event. Wire handlers via {{on 'invalid' this.handler}}.

Label.notes: text maps to the label-text named slot: text. For plain string labels, the label attribute can be used instead: label='text'. Prefer the slot when the label content contains HTML or components.

HelperText.notes: text maps to the helper-text named slot: text. For plain strings, the helperText property can be used instead. Prefer the slot for rich content.

Error.notes: text maps to the validity-message named slot: text. For plain strings, use the invalid-text attribute instead. Populating this slot or attribute is what triggers the invalid visual state — there is no separate invalid boolean. If Field.Error uses [E].Message to iterate multiple messages, concatenate them into a single validity-message slot.

CharacterCount.notes: <Field.CharacterCount> maps to CWC's built-in character counter: add enable-counter boolean attribute and max-count attribute (required for the counter to display) on cds-text-input. Example: <cds-text-input enable-counter max-count='200'>. The counter display is automatic — no custom slot needed.

Hds::Form::TextInput::Field.notes: Confidence raised to 0.85. Key corrections: (1) @isInvalid maps directly to the invalid boolean attribute on cds-text-input — it exists and reflects; (2) @hasVisibilityToggle defaults are INVERTED — HDS defaults true, CWC defaults false; add show-password-visibility-toggle explicitly for password fields; (3) Field.CharacterCount now has a direct CWC equivalent: enable-counter + max-count attributes; (4) @visibilityToggleAriaMessageText has no CWC equivalent — remove; (5) showPasswordLabel/hidePasswordLabel are JS-property-only (no HTML attribute) — must be set programmatically; (6) [E].Message (multiple error iteration) must be flattened to a single validity-message slot.

Hds::Button.description: Primary button component with various styles and sizes

@text.notes: @text (required) becomes the default slot content of cds-button. If @isIconOnly is true, @text is used as the tooltip label (tooltip-text attribute) rather than visible text.

@color.notes: HDS @color ('primary', 'secondary', 'tertiary', 'critical') maps to kind on cds-button. 'critical' → 'danger'. CWC also supports 'ghost', 'danger-tertiary', 'danger-ghost' which have no HDS equivalent.

@size.notes: CWC size values are xs, sm, md, lg (default), xl, 2xl. HDS 'medium' (default) maps to CWC 'lg' (default) — NOT 'md'. HDS 'small' → 'sm'. HDS 'large' → 'xl'. Note: CWC 'md' is a size smaller than 'lg' with no direct HDS equivalent.

@isFullWidth.notes: @isFullWidth renders the button filling its container width. cds-button has no fullwidth attribute — remove and apply width: 100% via CSS on the cds-button element. Do NOT use isExpressive — that controls button height, not width.

@isInline.notes: @isInline renders the button as inline-block. cds-button renders inline by default — remove this attribute, no CWC equivalent needed.

@icon.notes: @icon is an HDS icon name string. Replace with a Carbon SVG element placed in slot='icon' on cds-button. No automatic string-to-SVG mapping exists — manual substitution required.

@iconPosition.notes: IMPORTANT: cds-button in v2.60.0 has NO icon-position attribute. The shadow DOM template always renders <slot></slot><slot name='icon'></slot> — the icon is always trailing (after text). If @iconPosition='trailing' (the HDS default), no action needed — that is the natural CWC layout. If @iconPosition='leading', there is no direct CWC attribute equivalent; workaround via CSS: apply display:flex; flex-direction:row-reverse on the cds-button element, or use CSS targeting slot order. Note: a tertiary button requires an icon per HDS WCAG guidance — ensure the icon slot is populated.

@isIconOnly.notes: When @isIconOnly is true, prefer Carbon's dedicated cds-icon-button rather than treating it as a normal cds-button. Use @text as the accessible label / tooltip content, substitute the HDS icon with a Carbon SVG, and map visual kind carefully because icon-only buttons do not support danger variants.

@href.notes: When @href is present, HDS Button renders as an <a>. cds-button also renders as <a> when href is set. CWC also supports download, hreflang, ping, rel, and target on the anchor.

@isHrefExternal.notes: @isHrefExternal={{true}} sets target='_blank' AND rel='noopener noreferrer' on HDS. On cds-button, set both target='_blank' and rel='noopener noreferrer' explicitly — CWC does not add rel automatically.

@route.notes: @route (and related args: @models, @model, @query, @current-when, @replace, @isRouteExternal) are Ember LinkTo routing args. cds-button has no routing — replace with href pointing to the resolved URL.

icon.notes: Carbon SVG placed in slot='icon' renders inside the button. Required when @isIconOnly is true. Optional alongside text content when @icon is set.

default.notes: Visible button text. Omit when using icon-only mode (use tooltip-text for the accessible label instead).

Hds::Button.notes: High confidence for standard text buttons — auto-apply eligible. Manual cases (noted here, not blocking): @icon requires a manual HDS icon name → Carbon SVG substitution (no automatic mapping); @isIconOnly should prefer cds-icon-button with tooltip/accessible label wiring; @isHrefExternal must set both target='_blank' AND rel='noopener noreferrer' explicitly; @route/routing args must be resolved to a plain href; @isFullWidth → CSS only. Key corrections from API review: (1) @color='critical' maps to kind='danger' for standard buttons; icon-only buttons do not support danger variants and need manual review; (2) @size HDS 'medium' → CWC 'lg' (NOT 'md'); (3) cds-button has NO icon-position attribute — icon always renders trailing; @iconPosition='leading' requires CSS workaround.

Hds::ButtonSet.description: Button grouping layout wrapper. HDS has no args. CWC adds one: stacked (boolean, vertical arrangement).

stacked.notes: CWC-only attribute — no HDS equivalent. cds-button-set is horizontal by default. Add stacked to arrange buttons vertically. Only add this if the design calls for a vertical stack.

default.notes: cds-button children are placed directly inside cds-button-set. IMPORTANT: cds-button-set auto-overrides the kind attribute on child cds-button elements on slotchange — first button is forced to 'secondary', all remaining buttons are forced to 'primary'. Do NOT rely on explicit kind values on the buttons to survive; the set overrides them. Use cds-modal-footer-button instead of cds-button when the set is inside a cds-modal-footer.

Hds::ButtonSet.notes: High confidence — near-direct tag rename. HdsButtonSet has no args. CWC adds stacked (boolean, vertical layout) which has no HDS equivalent — omit unless vertical stacking is needed. IMPORTANT behavioral difference: cds-button-set forces kind on child buttons (first → secondary, rest → primary) — any explicit kind values on children will be overridden. Example: <cds-button-set><cds-button>Cancel</cds-button><cds-button>Save</cds-button></cds-button-set> — kind is auto-applied.
